meta.title: GitPress — your blog, your repo
meta.description: GitPress.net is a writing tool, not a host. Posts, images, and drafts live in your GitHub repos. We only store account and site pointers.

common.buildStarted: GitHub has the data and is building. You can leave this page.
common.savedRebuild: Saved. The site will update in about a minute.

login.lead: Sign in to create a blog that lives on your own GitHub.
login.unconfigured: No sign-in providers are configured. Add at least one OAuth app in .env.local (see .env.example).
login.independent: Sign-in is separate from GitHub repo access. You can log in with Google, then connect GitHub.
login.githubSwitch: A browser that already authorized GitHub may skip the prompt. To switch GitHub accounts, sign out at github.com first, then come back.
login.pendingGithub: After you sign in, we’ll finish connecting the GitHub App you just installed.

dashboard.title: My sites
dashboard.emptyBody: Create a blog. Posts go into your own GitHub repository.
dashboard.permissionsUpdated: GitHub App permissions were updated. If Recent builds still says access is missing, refresh once.

newSite.name: Site name *
newSite.slugHint: Creates a public repo named slug and a private slug-data repo.
newSite.connectBody: GitPress needs the GitHub App to create two repos under your account: a private data repo (posts and drafts) and a public site repo (compiled pages). Choose All repositories so new repos are authorized automatically.
newSite.connectMissing: The GitHub App is not configured (GITHUB_APP_SLUG and related env vars). See apps/web/.env.example.
newSite.emptyHint: After GitHub is connected, you can have a blog on your own repos in seconds.
newSite.themeHint: You can switch later. Content is never affected.

settings.title: Settings
settings.accountLead: These settings follow your account and apply to every site you own. You don’t need to go back to My sites to change them.
settings.aiLeadBefore: Used for excerpts and first drafts in the post editor. Any OpenAI-compatible API works. See
settings.hostingLeadBefore: Compiled pages live in the public repo
settings.hostingLeadAfter: . GitHub Pages is the default. Pick a host and how to attach a domain under Site URL above.
settings.rotateLead: If Recent builds stays <fail>failed</fail>, or the site repo never grows past the initial README, the deploy key is often the problem. The button below regenerates it and starts a rebuild. Your posts are not touched.
settings.rotateHintBefore: Then wait about 1–2 minutes for GitHub Actions. Check Recent builds on the dashboard. If that view says Actions permission is missing, open
settings.gapLead: The install on {account} is not aligned with the App’s current scopes (still missing: {missing}). GitHub requires the account owner to confirm once. GitPress cannot grant this for you.
settings.noGapLead: This install looks complete. If build history is missing, or you just added scopes on GitHub, walk through the confirmation page again.
settings.githubAppHint: Opens GitHub’s install settings. If you see a yellow Review request or a new permission list, click Accept — no reinstall.
settings.author: Author (optional)
settings.authorPlaceholder: For copyright credit, not a GitHub username
settings.authorHint: Leave blank and the footer uses the site name. Don’t put your GitHub login if you don’t want it public.
settings.timezoneHint: The public site shows dates in this zone. Older posts without a zone also use it for “is it due yet.” The editor still uses your computer’s local time.
settings.convertUploadsToWebp: Convert JPEG/PNG to WebP on upload
settings.convertUploadsToWebpHint: On by default. GIF, SVG, and files that are already WebP or AVIF are skipped. If the browser cannot convert, conversion fails, or the WebP is not smaller, the original file is uploaded. Videos are never converted.
settings.beianLead: Fill this in if a mainland-China site must show an ICP number. Leave blank otherwise. It appears at the end of the footer and survives theme switches.
settings.gonganHint: Digits only, or the full “X公网安备 …号”. The footer shows the official badge and links to the lookup.
settings.aiBaseHint: Any OpenAI-compatible API: OpenAI, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Qwen, OpenRouter, and others.
settings.aiKeyKeep: Already set. Leave blank to keep it.
settings.aiKeyHint: Stored encrypted. Nobody, including us, can read the plaintext in the database.
settings.scratchHint: Shows at the top of the dashboard for todos and outlines. The text lives on the GitPress control plane, not in your content repo, and saving it does not start a build. Turning it off keeps the text; turning it back on restores it.
settings.hideGitpressBody: This footer line is how visitors find GitPress. Themes and the build tool are open source, and posts live on your GitHub. More people using it is what keeps this control plane worth running — so your Save button still has somewhere to land. Feel free to point friends who want a self-hosted blog to gitpress.net.
settings.hideGitpressOk: You can hide it. The site still builds.
settings.footerOrderHint: List order is footer order. Copyright defaults to the site name, never your GitHub username. Turning RSS off only hides the link; the feed is still generated.
settings.footerEmpty: Footer list is empty. An ICP number, if filled in, still appears at the end.
settings.menuOrderHint: List order is header order. Removed items leave the nav (category archives and standalone pages themselves are unchanged).
settings.menuEmpty: Menu is empty. The site will show no header links.
settings.catOrderHint: List order is header order. Categories hidden from the nav still get archive pages.
settings.noCats: No categories yet. Add one to shape the site sections.
settings.catNavOff: Hidden from the header; archive pages still exist
settings.savedNav: Saved. Navigation will update in about a minute.

landing.h1b: Keep posts on your own GitHub.
landing.lead: GitPress is a blog admin. You sign in and write. The words go into your GitHub repo. On save they become a static site on GitHub Pages. gitpress.net is the remote; readers never hit our servers.
landing.previewAlt: GitPress admin dashboard: sidebar, scratch notes, post counts, theme, and GitHub Actions usage
landing.statsNote: Public platform stats · refresh every 5 minutes · totals only, no personal data
landing.ossH2b: your blog stays in your repos.
landing.ossLead: Posts, images, and drafts never entered our database. Themes and the build tool are MIT. Compiles run on GitHub Actions, not our machines. The control plane is source-available (PolyForm Shield): self-host for yourself, don’t run a public competing platform. If we disappear, keep building with the same repos and Action. You are not migrating. You already have the files.
landing.ossPlatformKicker: Main repo · the site you click
landing.ossPlatformBody: WordPress-style admin: sign in, create repos, write, save. This is the control plane, not your article library. Source-available, PolyForm Shield.
landing.ossThemesBody: How a blog looks, how Markdown is written, the data-repo template. Switching or authoring a theme follows this spec.
landing.ossBuildBody: Reads the private data repo, builds a static site, pushes the public site repo. You can run the same Action in your own workflows.
landing.ossSeeAlso: What the three pieces do: <what></what>. What the control plane keeps: <privacy></privacy>.
landing.stepsLead: No server, database, or WordPress plugins to maintain. GitHub is the backend.
landing.step1Body: Use Google, GitHub, or another provider, install the GitPress App, and let us create repos for you.
landing.step2Body: Fill in site details, choose a builtin Astro theme, then write, upload media, and manage categories.
landing.step3Body: Every save triggers Actions. Compiled output is pushed to the public site repo. Pages is live.
landing.reposLead: Content and the website are split. Everything you write in the admin goes into the private data repo. Only compiled HTML/CSS/assets enter the public site repo for Pages.
landing.repoSite: Site repo (public) — Astro output; rebuild anytime to change theme
landing.repoActions: GitHub Actions — push triggers the build; our servers stay idle
landing.f1Body: Posts, images, and drafts live only in your private GitHub repo. GitPress.net is not a content library. Uninstall the App and we cannot read your prose.
landing.f2Body: One repo for posts and drafts, one for compiled pages. Changing theme is a config change. You don’t lose a word.
landing.f3Body: GitHub Actions compiles. GitHub Pages or Vercel hosts for free. There is no day the box won’t boot.
landing.f4Body: WordPress-style: dashboard, posts, media, appearance, settings. Almost no learning curve.
landing.aiTitle: Make your own theme with AI
landing.aiLead: You don’t need a design system. Copy our first prompt, let your AI ask questions, then generate an Astro theme GitPress can import.
landing.ai1Body: Open “Make a theme with AI” in Help and send the full prompt as the first message.
landing.ai2Body: The AI asks about style, layout, logo, and options. It writes code only after you answer.
landing.ai3Body: Push the theme to a public GitHub repo and paste the URL under Appearance. A store is coming.
landing.readyTitle: Ready for a blog you actually own?
landing.readyBody: Free to sign up. The prose is on your GitHub, not on GitPress.net servers. {users} users and {sites} sites already.

helpIndex.title: Questions authors actually ask
helpIndex.lead: Start with “What is GitPress?” to see how it differs from WordPress, Hugo, and VitePress. The rest is admin how-to, not a separate docs site.
helpIndex.searchPlaceholder: Search: what is this, privacy, drafts, builds, themes…
helpIndex.empty: No matching articles. Try another word, or clear the search.

whatIs.title: What is GitPress?
whatIs.summary: GitPress is a blog admin: write like WordPress, keep posts on your GitHub, publish a static site. Who it’s for, vs Hugo / WordPress / VitePress, and why it exists.
whatIs.keywords: intro what open source gitpress WordPress Hugo VitePress SSG

privacy.title: Privacy: what we keep
privacy.summary: Accounts and site pointers live on the control plane. Prose, media, and public HTML stay on your GitHub. Uninstall the App and we cannot read content.
privacy.keywords: privacy storage prose server Postgres auth

makeTheme.title: Make a theme with AI
makeTheme.summary: Copy the first prompt, let your AI ask questions then generate an Astro theme, push it, and import it under Appearance.

drafts.title: Scratch, drafts, and published
drafts.summary: Scratch notes stay in this browser. Drafts are committed to the private repo and built, but never appear on the public site. Scheduled posts need the publish check turned on.

builds.title: How builds run
builds.summary: After save, data is already in the private repo. Actions builds from there and pushes the public site repo. You can leave. A newer save cancels an in-flight run.
builds.keywords: build Actions data repo cancel queue

aiWriting.title: AI drafts and summaries
aiWriting.summary: Generate a Markdown draft in the editor, preview, then insert. Configure your own AI endpoint first.

importTheme.title: Import a theme from GitHub
importTheme.summary: Add a public repo to this site’s imports. Actions fetches and compiles it only after you enable it.

analytics.title: How to see traffic
analytics.summary: Connect GA, Clarity, Umami, and others on the analytics page. Config lives in the data repo; numbers live in each vendor’s dashboard.

domain.title: Use your own domain
domain.summary: Apex or subdomain. Follow GitHub Pages, Vercel, Cloudflare, or other hosts.

github.banner: GitHub App permissions changed. {account} has not approved them yet{suffix}. Confirm on GitHub — about 10 seconds.

themes.classic: Warm serif type, centered layout, classic blog feel.
themes.ink: Dark magazine cards. For night owls.

themes.showPostTime: Show time of day on posts

ops.title: Ops
ops.bar: Platform ops · metadata only, never the author’s admin
ops.homeLead: Control-plane metadata. Posts, images, and AI key plaintext are not here.
ops.usersLead: Accounts and site counts. Operators do not enter someone else’s /sites/… admin, and AI keys stay encrypted.
ops.revokeHint: Clearing the database role still leaves GITPRESS_OPS_EMAILS in effect
ops.usersFoot: Up to 300 rows. Created-at is not on the user table (Auth.js has no createdAt).
ops.sitesLead: Metadata and public links only. Ops cannot open someone else’s writing admin.
ops.sitesFoot: Theme source is stored from this launch. Sites imported from GitHub earlier that never switched themes may still show builtin.
ops.installsLead: GitHub App install mapping. User-to-server tokens are not shown.
ops.storeLead: The catalog is GitHub pointers, not zip files. Builtin themes come from tap6/gitpress@v1 and are not in this table.
ops.emptyCatalog: No store entries yet. Listed themes appear on owners’ Appearance pages.
ops.confirmDeleteListing: Remove “{name}” from the catalog? Sites already using it are unaffected.
ops.listingHint: Stores a pointer github:owner/repo#ref. Theme files stay in that repo. The owner’s GitHub Actions clone them; nothing is installed on GitPress servers.

hosting.fillVisitorUrl: Set the URL visitors will open first

hosting.whichHost: Which host is this site on?
hosting.whichHostHint: Saving with GitHub Pages registers the domain with GitHub. Saving with another host unregisters it from Pages and only updates the visitor URL.

history.title: Git history
history.editorEmptyFile: After you save to the repo, this file’s changes show up here.
history.editorEmptyCommits: This file has no commits of its own yet.
history.lead: Every save, theme switch, and settings change leaves a version in your private data repo. This list is plain language; open a row to see it on GitHub (the data repo is private).
history.sourceHint: (private data repo). The public site repo is compiled output; you usually don’t need it.
history.empty: Nothing yet. Save a post or change settings and it will show up here.

siteDash.title: Dashboard
siteDash.created: Site created. The first build is running on GitHub Actions and is usually live in 1–2 minutes.
siteDash.drafts: Drafts (in the private repo, hidden on the public site)
siteDash.usageHint: Builds run on the private data repo and count toward GitHub’s monthly free minutes. Public repos don’t. GitPress commits images with the post so each image doesn’t trigger its own build.
siteDash.usageNoPerm: This install can’t read Actions yet, so we can’t total this site’s build minutes.
siteDash.billingUnavailable: The GitHub App can’t read account totals; use the billing page.
siteDash.runningHint: Usually 1–2 minutes · this page refreshes every 5 seconds
siteDash.noActionsPerm: This GitHub App install has no Actions scope, so we can’t list runs here (saves still trigger builds).
siteDash.bannerOr: Use the banner at the top or
siteDash.reviewNew: approve the new permissions on GitHub

editor.postSlugPlaceholder: URL slug (leave blank to generate from the title; English is best)
editor.pageSlugPlaceholder: URL slug, e.g. about (leave blank to generate). Public URL is /slug/
editor.postSlugHint: Changing this creates a redirect from the old URL. The filename stays; the public path becomes /posts/new-slug/.
editor.pageSlugHint: Changing this creates a redirect. Header and footer items that point here will follow.
editor.statusDraft: Draft · not public (in the private repo, hidden on the public site)
editor.draftHint: Save writes the private repo and starts a build, but this post will not appear on the public site.
editor.publishHint: After save it will appear on the public site.
editor.scheduleOff: Scheduled publishing is off, so the date cannot be in the future. To book a time, open <link>Settings → Scheduled posts</link>.
editor.pageNoDraft: Pages have no draft status. After save they appear at
editor.implicitNavHint: Until you save a custom menu, every page appears in the header. To show only some pages, save a menu once.
editor.pendingTitle: This browser has an unsaved local note
editor.pendingSuffix: . What you wrote before switching tabs or refreshing is still here.
editor.localDraftPostHint: {saved} · only on this browser. Save to write the repo.
editor.localDraftPageHint: {saved} · only on this browser. Save to GitHub before it appears on the site.
editor.localDraftFail: Could not write the local note (storage may be full). Save to GitHub soon.
editor.pendingImagesHint: Images are previewed locally. They go into the data repo with the post when you save, in one build.
editor.trayTitle: Waiting to save with the post
editor.trayQueued: Preview inserted. Save to write the repo.
editor.aiLead: Preview first, then insert. Nothing is saved to the repo yet.
editor.aiTopicPlaceholder: e.g. a weekend at the coast, with a bit of weather and food

media.title: Media library
media.lead: Images and common short videos (mp4/webm/mov) can be previewed. Files live in media/ in the private data repo and appear at /media/... on the public site after a build.
media.uploadHint: 8MB per file. Library uploads write the repo and start a build right away. Images inserted while writing wait until you save the post.
media.uploadConvertOn: JPEG and PNG are converted to WebP in the browser on upload (GIF, SVG, and existing WebP/AVIF are left alone).
media.uploadConvertOff: Original files are kept; WebP conversion is off.
media.empty: Library is empty. After you upload, click a thumbnail or Preview for a full view.
media.logoHint: Shows in the header; themes can hide it. A PNG/JPG with a transparent or light background works well.
media.avatarHint: Round avatar. Hidden by default; turn on Show avatar under Appearance.

appearance.title: Appearance · themes
appearance.lead: A theme only changes presentation. Posts and images stay in the data repo. Open a card for details; Enable is what rebuilds the site.
appearance.footnote: Listed themes are curated in ops. You can also add any public GitHub repo to this site. Want to make your own? The DIY theme guide includes a complete first prompt for your AI.
appearance.officialHint: GitPress builtin themes. Builds pull them from tap6/gitpress@v1.
appearance.listedHint: Community themes accepted for the catalog. Your Actions clone them from GitHub after you enable one.
appearance.mineEmptyHint: Add a public GitHub theme to this site’s list, then enable it when you want. Nothing is written to the content repo.
appearance.mineHint: Visible only on this site. Removing from the list does not delete the GitHub theme.
appearance.mineEmpty: No imported themes yet. Use the form below.
appearance.importHint: The repo must be public, with a spec v1 theme.json at the root or subdirectory. Adding only records it here; Enable is when Actions clones it.
appearance.added: Added to My imports: {name}. Open the card and Enable to rebuild.
appearance.author: Author
appearance.switchHint: Enabling another theme rebuilds with that theme’s defaults. Accent color and similar options do not carry over.
appearance.footnoteBefore: Listed themes are curated in ops. You can also add any public GitHub repo to this site. Want to make your own? See
appearance.footnoteAfter: — it includes a complete first prompt for your AI.

posts.title: Posts
posts.savedDraft: Saved to the private data repo. A build still runs, but this draft will not appear on the public site.
posts.saved: Saved to the data repo. The site will update in about a minute.
posts.footnote: There are two statuses: Published appears on the public site; Draft writes the private data repo and starts a build, but stays off the public site. A static blog has no login, so there is no third “private to me” status.
posts.bulkDraft: Set draft (hidden on the public site)
posts.bulkHint: Select posts to change status or delete
posts.confirmDelete: Delete {n} selected post(s)? This removes the files from the data repo.
posts.empty: No posts yet. Click Write to start.
posts.draftTitle: Drafts write the private repo and start a build, but stay off the public site
posts.scheduleOffQuick: Scheduled publishing is off, so you cannot pick a future time.

pages.title: Pages
pages.saved: Saved to the data repo. The site will update in about a minute.
pages.footnote: Pages are site furniture (about, contact, privacy). They live at the root, e.g. /about/. Posts are what show on the home page and in RSS.
pages.empty: No pages yet. Click Write to start. About is created when the site is.
pages.confirmDelete: Delete page “{title}”? This removes the file from the data repo.

categoriesPage.title: Categories
categoriesPage.lead: Keep an ordered category list. Posts pick one on the edit screen, and the public site gets an archive per category. The header-nav switch only applies until you save a Menu; after that the menu page is the only source. Turning a switch off is not a delete — archives and post assignment stay. Free-form tags are unchanged.

menuPage.title: Menu
menuPage.lead: Choose what the header shows, in what order, and with which labels — including whether Home appears. You can override each label (Home → Home, or a local word). RSS belongs in the footer by default; add + RSS if you still want it in the header. Footer items, copyright, and ICP live in Settings. After you save, the header shows only this list, and the category “header nav” switches no longer apply.
menuPage.firstOpen: This is the first time you open the menu editor. It is prefilled from the theme default and takes effect after you save.

analyticsPage.title: Analytics
analyticsPage.leadBefore: GitPress does not store visitors or draw its own charts. Config lives in your private data repo; only items marked Embed in site are inserted. Turning a box off keeps the IDs, and the next build simply omits the script. Numbers live in each vendor’s dashboard. See

aiPage.title: AI settings
aiPage.leadBefore: Configure once and every site’s editor can generate excerpts and first drafts. You can also change this under any site’s Settings → Account. See

comments.lead: Comments take two steps. Installing the giscus App first, then connecting is the reliable order — the reverse still works. Installing the App does not rebuild; writing the connection does.
comments.needDiscussions: Connecting needs the GitPress App’s Discussions permission. Please
comments.reviewInPage: approve the new permission under Troubleshooting · GitHub App on this page.
comments.appMissing: Config is written, but this repo still lacks the giscus App. Opening a post shows “giscus is not installed on this repository”. Finish step 1, then refresh the post — no extra build.
comments.saved: Saved. The site will update in about a minute.
comments.step1Body: Authorize giscus on the public repo <repo></repo>. Without it visitors only see an error and cannot comment.
comments.step2Body: GitPress opens Discussions and writes the repo / category IDs. A build is queued so the comment box appears on posts.
comments.connectEarly: You can connect now, but the post page will still say it is not installed until step 1 is done.
comments.step3Body: Turning this off only hides the box. Config stays; you don’t have to start over.

publish.title: Scheduled-post checks
publish.lead: When this is off you cannot pick a future date. When it is on, GitHub checks on an interval — not at the exact minute.
publish.otherSites: GitHub account {account} has {n} other site(s). Private-repo Actions minutes are one shared pool.
publish.othersLater: After you turn this on, other sites that enable checks will add to the same pool.
publish.intervalHint: The usual single-site suggestion is every 2 hours. If quota is plentiful, the estimator may suggest 1 hour.
publish.notExactBody: After the date, wait up to one more interval (now: {hint}).
publish.alwaysRunsBody: Once on, builds run on the interval. Typing does not use minutes; Save does.
publish.eachRunBody: . Sites on the same account share the quota. A coarser delay leaves more minutes for saves.
publish.quotaSaves: . Keeping 80% free for saves, about {n} saves left.
publish.overCaution: Over {percent}%. You’ll be asked to confirm before saving.
publish.chartPrivate: Each interval plus other sites, as a share of quota
publish.chartPublic: Estimated checks per interval (public repos usually don’t use the 2000)
publish.savesAsk: About how many saves will this site make per month? (Edits count. Typing and local notes don’t. Optional.)
publish.dailySavesEmpty: : leave blank to skip this term. Typing does not use Actions.
publish.savesLeft: Leaving 80% for saves, this interval still has about {n} saves.
publish.savesOver: The number you entered is already above that. Pick a coarser interval.
publish.accountUsed: This account has used about {n} minutes this month (not the same ledger as the monthly projection).
publish.recommendEmpty: With no save count, the suggestion is based on checks only.
publish.recommendFilled: The suggestion subtracts the saves you entered, then sees how dense checks can be.
publish.recommendHint: Spare quota can go to 1 hour. Other sites or frequent saves push it coarser. Current suggestion: {label}.
publish.banner: {n} published post(s) still have a future date, but scheduled checks are off, so they will not appear on their own. Open <link>Settings → Scheduled posts</link>, or save / rebuild after the date.

domain.why1Title: 1. Tell GitPress the new address first
domain.why1: Links, images, and CSS paths are written at compile time. If visitors open example.com, save that address in Settings (same for a subdomain — use the name they actually type). Changing DNS alone can load HTML while images and CSS still point at the old github.io host.
domain.why2Title: 2. Attach the domain at the host
domain.why2: Compiled pages live in the public site repo (not the -data one). Add the domain in whichever static host you use. GitPress does not manage Cloudflare or Vercel DNS. Use the buttons below for the matching steps.
domain.apexHint: The name you bought, used as the site
domain.subHint: One extra label in front, including www
domain.multiSitesTitle: Several sites, each with its own apex
domain.multiSites: Site A on example.com, site B on another.com. On GitHub Pages the DNS values can be identical (both point at Pages). GitHub cares which site repo registered the name — don’t put the repo name in DNS.
domain.pagesLead: Keep the GitHub Pages host created with the site. GitPress can register the domain with GitHub for you.
domain.pagesStepSettings: Enter the visitor address (usually example.com) and save. We register it with GitHub Pages and start a rebuild.
domain.pagesStepHelp: Admin → Settings → Site URL, choose GitHub Pages, enter the visitor address (usually example.com), save.
domain.pagesDnsStep: Add the records at your DNS host. Apex and subdomain syntax differ.
domain.pagesDnsGenerated: This table is generated from the domain already registered.
domain.cfGrey: If DNS is at Cloudflare, records that point at Pages must be DNS only (grey cloud). Orange proxy blocks GitHub from issuing a certificate.
domain.vercelLead: Point the same static files at Vercel and add the domain in the Vercel console.
domain.vercel1: In Vercel, Import the public site repo. Do not import the -data repo — that is the private posts repo.
domain.vercel2: Framework: Other. Leave Build Command empty. Output Directory: . The repo already has HTML. Do not run another build.
domain.vercel3: Project Settings → Domains: add your domain. Apex uses the ALIAS / A records Vercel gives you; subdomains are usually CNAME to cname.vercel-dns.com.
domain.vercel4Settings: Back here, save the same visitor address. Saving unregisters it from GitHub Pages.
domain.vercel4Help: Back in GitPress Settings, choose Vercel, enter the same address, save.
domain.dontBothVercel: The same hostname cannot point at Pages and Vercel. Choosing Vercel here and saving unregisters Pages. You can also unregister first, then add the domain in Vercel.
domain.cfLead: Use Cloudflare Pages. Certificates and DNS are handled by Cloudflare.
domain.cf1: Cloudflare Dashboard → Workers & Pages, connect the site repo. Turn the build off (or output the repo root).
domain.cf2: Custom domains: apex, subdomain, or multi-level. Use the records Cloudflare generates. Orange cloud is fine here; Cloudflare issues the cert.
domain.cf3Settings: Back here, save the same visitor address. Don’t choose GitHub Pages; saving unregisters Pages.
domain.cf3Help: Back in GitPress Settings, choose Cloudflare, enter the same address, save.
domain.dontBothCf: Cloudflare can proxy; GitHub Pages cannot. Keep one hostname on one host. Choosing Cloudflare and saving unregisters Pages.
domain.otherLead: Netlify, your own Nginx, object storage plus CDN — same idea: the host that serves the files owns the domain.
domain.other1: Deploy the site repo to your static host (again, not the -data repo).
domain.other2: Follow that host’s docs to add the domain, write DNS, and wait for a certificate.
domain.other3Settings: Back here, save the full visitor address.
domain.other3Help: Back in GitPress Settings, choose Other, enter the same address, save.
domain.apexDns: Host record @. Most DNS hosts do not allow a CNAME on the apex, so use A / AAAA to GitHub Pages:
domain.subDns: One CNAME is enough. Host is the labels in front of the apex. Value is username.github.io — no repo name.
domain.subDnsFoot: Maps to blog.example.com, www.example.com, docs.blog.example.com. Check with: dig +short CNAME blog.example.com
domain.pit1Title: DNS changed, visitor address not saved
domain.pit1: The page may load while assets still point at /repo-name/.... Save the domain in Settings and wait for that build.
domain.pit2: Most DNS hosts reject a CNAME on @. Use A / AAAA for the apex; CNAME only for subdomains.
domain.pit3Title: Pages and another host fighting over the name
domain.pit3: Unregister Pages in Settings, then add the domain in Vercel / Cloudflare. Two GitPress sites should not register the same hostname.
domain.pit4Title: DNS is right, site is still 404
domain.pit4: The rebuild is probably still running. Check GitPress Build on the data repo’s Actions tab.
domain.helpLead: Most people use the apex they bought as the site address — example.com for site A, another.com for site B. A subdomain (blog.example.com) or extra labels work too. In Settings, save the name visitors actually type.
domain.pickLevelHint: Apex is recommended; extra prefixes use the same steps.
domain.pickHost: Pick a host and follow its steps
domain.pickHostHint: Don’t point the same name at two hosts.
domain.fillFirstTitle: Save the address visitors will open
domain.fillFirst: Links and CSS paths are written at compile time. After you switch to your own domain, you must save it here once.
domain.whichHostHint: GitHub Pages: saving registers the domain with GitHub. Other hosts: saving unregisters Pages and only updates the visitor address.
domain.stillOnPagesTitle: This domain is still registered on GitHub Pages
domain.stillOnPages: Saving will unregister Pages so two hosts don’t fight over the certificate. To free the name first, you can also unregister Pages below.
domain.visitorHint: Prefer the apex, e.g. example.com. Subdomains work too, e.g. blog.example.com. To go back to default Pages, save the default URL.
domain.noticeUrl: Site address updated and a rebuild started. Attach the same domain in your host’s console.
domain.noticePages: Address updated and registered with GitHub Pages. Add the DNS rows from the table.
domain.noticeReset: Back to the default Pages address {url}
domain.noticeUnpages: Pages registration removed. The visitor address is unchanged. Point DNS at the host you use now.
